40388-the-life-of-john-marshall-volume-1:
Albert J Beveridge wrote The Life of John Marshall, with volume one dated by its rights pages to nineteen sixteen and nineteen nineteen. Marshall was the great chief justice of the United States. This volume covers his years as frontiersman, soldier, and lawmaker, from seventeen fifty-five to seventeen eighty-eight.

Beveridge opens with ancestry and setting, from Braddock's defeat to colonial Virginia life. He notes Marshall's kinship with Jefferson and the weight of slavery on that world. A frontier schooling follows, in a little house in the Hollow by the Blue Ridge. Marshall's joy in nature and his father's training shape the portrait.
50369-men-of-mawm:
Riley wrote this Yorkshire novel of men of the moorland country he loved. Maniwel Drake, who has lost an arm, keeps a cheerful and genial nature in the tale. Baldwin Briggs, whose motto is all for himself, stands against him, the book's own summary says at the front.

Riley had forsaken the white rose for the red in one earlier book, that summary notes. He returns here to his own country and to contrasts of character he loved to draw. Dramatic episodes and character studies mix in the story, and above all the breath of the moors blows through it, without which no book of his would be itself.
65236-roster-of-the-rainbow-division-for:
Harold Stanley Johnson, a lieutenant of the 151st Field Artillery, edited and compiled this roster of the Rainbow Division, the Forty Second Division of the American army, copyrighted in 1917. The division's commander, Major General Mann, receives the dedication. Johnson dates his work from Camp Mills, Long Island, in October 1917.

The roster lists the division's whole order of battle. Headquarters troop came from Louisiana cavalry, the signal battalion from Missouri, the supply train from Texas. The artillery brigade joins regiments from Illinois, Indiana, and Minnesota. The infantry brigades pair the famous 69th New York with Ohio and Wisconsin regiments. The Rainbow Division was built from National Guard units of twenty six states, and the roster is its birth certificate.
